101.name: RADIO_DEAF
101.title: Radio heard no Wi-Fi networks at boot
101.cause: The boot-time scan found nothing on any channel. Seen on a used board whose saved flash data was stale; also a damaged or missing antenna.
101.fix: Wipe the board and reflash it. If it still hears nothing, inspect the antenna; replace the board if it is damaged.

102.name: RADIO_START_FAILED
102.title: ESP-NOW failed to start
102.cause: node.begin() failed: the Wi-Fi driver or ESP-NOW could not initialise.
102.fix: Usually transient; the bundled sketches restart themselves. If it persists, reflash with a wipe.

103.name: NO_COORDINATOR
103.title: No beacon from the coordinator for the failsafe period
103.cause: The node stopped hearing the coordinator and fell back to its safe state: out of range, the coordinator is down, or the swarm channel differs.
103.fix: Check the coordinator is running; move the node or add a relay; confirm every unit uses the same HW_SWARM_CHANNEL.

104.name: WEAK_LINK
104.title: Link to the hive weaker than -90 dBm
104.cause: The hive's own beacons, heard directly, arrive at the edge of range, so some traffic will be lost. Raised once when the link turns weak (and again every few hours while it stays weak); a node that only hears the hive through a relay does not raise it.
104.fix: Move the node or a relay closer, and keep metal and batteries away from the board's antenna.

201.name: FW_CRC_BAD
201.title: Firmware image refused: checksum mismatch
201.cause: An image arrived over ESP-NOW but did not match its CRC. The node kept running its current firmware.
201.fix: Push again. Repeated failures point at radio noise near the sender.

202.name: FW_TRANSFER_STALLED
202.title: Firmware transfer stalled and was abandoned
202.cause: The image stopped arriving part way. The node kept running its current firmware.
202.fix: Push again with the node closer to the sender, or through a relay.

203.name: FW_WRONG_FAMILY
203.title: Firmware image for a different node type, refused
203.cause: A push carried another family's image. Refusing it is correct.
203.fix: Nothing to fix: push the image built for this node's family.

204.name: FW_NO_SPACE
204.title: Firmware image too large for the update partition
204.cause: The image is bigger than the space the partition table leaves for an update.
204.fix: Build with a partition scheme that has an OTA slot large enough, or shrink the image.

205.name: FW_WRITE_FAILED
205.title: Firmware image could not be written or finalised
205.cause: The flash write came up short, or finishing the update failed. The node kept running its current firmware.
205.fix: Push again. If it repeats on one node only, its flash may be failing.

206.name: UPDATE_ROLLED_BACK
206.title: New firmware did not rejoin the swarm and was rolled back
206.cause: An update booted but never proved it could rejoin (or crashed repeatedly), so the node reverted to its previous image.
206.fix: The new image is faulty or mis-built (a different channel or protocol version?). Check it before pushing again.

207.name: OTA_WIFI_FAILED
207.title: Over-the-air Wi-Fi update could not complete
207.cause: Not configured, not armed, no Wi-Fi, a bad URL or a failed download.
207.fix: Check HW_OTA_SSID and HW_OTA_URL in the build, arm the node first, and that the image server is reachable.

301.name: PERIPHERAL_MISSING
301.title: A peripheral did not answer
301.cause: A sensor or device the application expects was not found. The subject says which slot it feeds.
301.fix: Check that device's power, ground and data wiring.

302.name: PERIPHERAL_READ_FAILED
302.title: A peripheral stopped answering
302.cause: The device was found earlier but a read failed. The slot's value is stale until it recovers.
302.fix: Reseat its connector. Repeated failures point at a loose wire or a damaged device.

303.name: INPUT_FLOATING
303.title: An input looks unconnected
303.cause: Consecutive samples disagreed far more than a connected source would: typically a floating analog pin.
303.fix: Check the wire to that input and that the device is powered.

304.name: VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE
304.title: A reading is outside its plausible range
304.cause: A steady value the connected device should never produce: shorted, mis-wired, or the wrong part.
304.fix: Check the wiring and that the part is the one the firmware expects.

305.name: BATTERY_LOW
305.title: Battery low
305.cause: The node's battery is nearly empty.

401.name: UNASSIGNED
401.title: Board has no node number yet
401.cause: It runs a generic image and waits to be given a number over USB. It will not join the swarm until then.
401.fix: Give it a number from the Flash page, or send `setid <n>` over its USB serial.

402.name: BAD_NODE_ID
402.title: Node number rejected
402.cause: A setid asked for a number outside 1-254.
402.fix: Use a number from 1 to 254 that no other node has.

501.name: UPLINK_DOWN
501.title: Gateway lost an uplink
501.cause: An uplink (LoRa, USB or HTTP) stopped answering. The subject names which.
501.fix: Check that uplink's cable or radio. For a Meshtastic uplink, see the README's notes on the Serial Module and GPS pin.

502.name: UNTRUSTED_COMMAND
502.title: Command from an untrusted source refused
502.cause: A command arrived somewhere it is not accepted from (for example another LoRa channel). Refusing it is correct.
502.fix: Nothing to fix unless it is you: send commands on the trusted channel.

601.name: GATEWAY_SILENT
601.title: Gateway not answering on USB
601.cause: The host's poll of the gateway failed: unplugged, reset, or its serial port is held by another program.
601.fix: Check the gateway's USB cable and that nothing else has its port open.

602.name: CLOCK_BEHIND
602.title: Host clock is behind, readings held
602.cause: The host booted with a stale clock and the time is earlier than readings already stored.
602.fix: Usually fixes itself once network time syncs. Check the host has internet or an NTP source.

603.name: UPLOAD_FAILED
603.title: Upload to an external service failed
603.cause: A batch of readings could not be delivered. It is kept and retried.
603.fix: Check the host's internet connection and the service's pairing.

604.name: FLASH_FAILED
604.title: Flashing a board failed
604.cause: The Flash page could not write or set up a board; its log says at which step.
604.fix: Replug the board with a data (not charge-only) USB cable and try again with a wipe.

605.name: HOST_UNDERVOLTAGE
605.title: Host power supply is too weak
605.cause: The host (a Raspberry Pi) reported undervoltage or throttling. USB devices on it make this worse, and it can corrupt the SD card.
605.fix: Use the host's official power supply, or a powered USB hub for the boards.

606.name: WRITE_NOT_APPLIED
606.title: A setting was sent but the node never confirmed it
606.cause: The gateway sent the write and re-sent it several times, but the node's reports never showed the new value: it is out of range, asleep, or only reachable through a relay (commands are not relayed yet).
606.fix: Check the node is up and how far it is from the gateway; try again when it is heard directly.
